doctrine: Community of Common Destiny & Major Country Diplomacy — China asserts its role as a leading global power offering alternative global governance (Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative) to Western institutional hegemony, emphasizing state sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, multi-polarity, and the primacy of the UN Charter.
strategic_priorities: Deter Taiwanese formal independence and prepare military, economic, and cyber capabilities for potential cross-strait reunification
Secure maritime control within the First Island Chain and construct an insurmountable A2/AD envelope deterring US naval power in the Western Pacific
Mitigate the 'Malacca Dilemma' by diversifying land-based energy pipelines (Russia, Central Asia) and developing Indian Ocean maritime outlets (Pakistan, Myanmar)
Deepen the comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination with Russia, consolidating northern border security and locking in low-cost energy flows
Establish technological autarky to survive potential Western sanctions, decoupling, and semiconductor export controls
priority_regions: East Asia & Western Pacific (Taiwan Strait, South China Sea, East China Sea, Korean Peninsula)
Central Asia & Russia (Eurasian heartland, SCO members, land corridors to Europe)
Southeast Asia / ASEAN (primary trading partner, maritime littorals, intermediate production networks)
Global South (Middle East, Africa, Latin America — resources, voting blocs in UN forums, BRI infrastructure)

cooperates_closely_with: Russia ('No-limits' comprehensive strategic partnership, military exercises, mutual UN veto alignment, energy pipeline integration)
Pakistan ('All-weather strategic cooperative partner', CPEC flagship, military co-production)
North Korea (sole formal mutual defense treaty partner under the 1961 Treaty of Friendship)
Iran (25-year comprehensive strategic cooperation agreement, primary purchaser of Iranian oil)
Global South / BRICS+ nations (alternative financial clearing mechanisms, infrastructure lending, commodity trade)
competes_or_disputes_with: United States (core structural geopolitical, military, technological, and ideological superpower rivalry across the Indo-Pacific)
India (disputed 3,488 km Himalayan LAC, competition for Indian Ocean naval influence, border infrastructure race)
Japan (Senkaku / Diaoyu Islands sovereignty dispute, East China Sea gas fields, Tokyo's expanding defense perimeter)
Taiwan (existential sovereignty dispute; Beijing asserts Taiwan is an inalienable province)
South China Sea claimant states (Philippines, Vietnam — overlapping EEZ and maritime feature claims)
cooperation_and_competition.notes: China's foreign policy has evolved under Xi Jinping from Deng Xiaoping's low-profile posture ('hide capabilities and bide time') into assertive major-country diplomacy ('dare to fight and dare to win'). Beijing leverages its colossal trading footprint and lending power to insulate itself against Western sanctions while promoting a multipolar international architecture.

_meta.data_quality: sourced/analytical synthesis based on PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Defense White Papers, and Chinese Communist Party Central Committee foreign affairs resolutions
